question: A case-control study finds that 40 out of 100 cancer patients were exposed to a toxin vs. 20 out of 100 controls. Compute the odds ratio (OR) and 95% CI.

files.eval_guideline: Odds ratio and CI bounds must match the reference within +/-0.05; column order and header labels may differ.
files.match_reasoning: Both files share the same name, odds_ratio_results.csv, and are CSVs. Each holds the odds ratio and 95% CI results for the case-control toxin task.

parameters.question: Compare odds ratio and 95% CI results for a case-control study (40/100 exposed cases vs 20/100 exposed controls). OR (~2.67) and lower/upper CI bounds must match the reference within +/-0.05; column order and header labels may differ.

files.strategy_reasoning: This is a deterministic calculation that produces a small results table (the OR and its 95% CI bounds). The guideline asks for a value-by-value match within ±0.05 and allows the column order and headers to differ, so approximate is the right fit.

align_plan.reasoning: Both tables hold one summary row, so they are not transposed versions of each other. The three reference columns (Odds_Ratio, CI_Lower, CI_Upper) have exact-name matches in the candidate, so they map one-to-one. The candidate's extra columns (2x2 cell counts, SE, CI method, p-values, chi-square) are not in the reference and are left out. With only one row there is no ID column to match on, so rows line up by position and no sorting or permutation check is needed. Values then get compared within the ±0.05 tolerance (e.g. 2.6667 vs 2.667, 1.4166 vs 1.417, 5.0199 vs 5.02).

column_configs.name: Odds_Ratio
column_configs.reasoning: This is the main result. The ±0.05 absolute tolerance, divided by the reference value 2.667, gives a relative tolerance of about 0.0187.

column_configs.name: CI_Lower
column_configs.reasoning: Lower CI bound. The ±0.05 absolute tolerance, divided by the reference value 1.417, gives a relative tolerance of about 0.0353.

column_configs.name: CI_Upper
column_configs.reasoning: Upper CI bound. The ±0.05 absolute tolerance, divided by the reference value 5.02, gives a relative tolerance of about 0.00996.

comparison_plan.overall_reasoning: The task asks for an odds ratio and its 95% CI, so only the three reference columns (Odds_Ratio, CI_Lower, CI_Upper) are compared. The candidate's extra columns (2x2 counts, SE, p-values, chi2, method) are not in the reference and are left out. The guideline sets an absolute tolerance of ±0.05, so I compare each column with RAE and convert that absolute tolerance into a relative one using the reference value: 0.05/2.667 ≈ 0.0187 for the OR, 0.05/1.417 ≈ 0.0353 for the lower bound, and 0.05/5.02 ≈ 0.00996 for the upper bound. The candidate values (2.6667, 1.4166, 5.0199) are well within these tolerances. Sign is meaningful, so compare_abs is false.
